idiom_name: interface struct of function pointers + a static const no-op instance
implementation_notes: C has no objects, so the collaborator interface becomes a struct of function pointers and the null object is a file-scope static instance whose pointers address no-op functions; callers receive that instance instead of NULL and call through the table. Nothing in the language supplies the pattern, so both the interface and the neutral implementation are hand-written - the pay-off is that the 'if (p) p->op(p)' guard disappears from every call site. Use it only when the null case is genuinely normal; otherwise return an error code or a bool out-parameter and let the caller branch.
pitfalls: A null function pointer is not a null object: calling through a NULL or uninitialised table entry is undefined behaviour, so every field of the shared instance must be filled in at compile time.
The instance must be static (one definition per program) and treated as immutable; a mutable shared null object is global state that any caller can corrupt.
The pattern does not remove the ownership question: the caller still has to know whether the instance it holds is heap-allocated or the shared static one.
